title: Heart failure: treatment and noticing change
intro: Heart failure means the heart cannot fill or pump effectively enough for the body’s needs. It is not the same as the heart stopping. Different forms need different treatment, and many people benefit from ongoing care.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Breathlessness with activity or lying down, fatigue and swelling may occur. Similar symptoms have other causes, so diagnosis requires assessment rather than judging only ankle swelling or an online checklist.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: Tests may include blood tests, an ECG and heart ultrasound to establish function and likely cause. Ask which type you have; a preserved pumping fraction does not rule out heart failure. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Medicines are chosen by type and associated illness; diuretics relieve fluid retention while other treatments may reduce deterioration or hospitalization. Devices or procedures help selected people. Blood pressure, kidney function and blood salts need monitoring. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Agree a plan for activity, rehabilitation, weight monitoring and whom to call for changes. Salt and fluid advice must be individualized; do not impose drastic restriction or change diuretic doses unless the team has provided a specific plan. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Rapid weight increase, worsening swelling or new breathlessness need prompt contact. Severe breathlessness at rest, chest pain, blue lips or collapse require emergency help. Avoid starting anti-inflammatory painkillers without checking because they may worsen fluid retention.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira records a rising weight and tighter shoes. She contacts the team using her written action plan rather than waiting for her routine visit.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben feels better on treatment but continues medicines and monitoring, knowing symptom relief does not mean the underlying condition has disappeared.
